title: Invocation Sanctuary: cross-protocol tool call adapter with progressive streaming and lenient param coercion
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We support multiple tool/function surfaces (OpenAI-style 'tools' JSON, legacy 'functions' RPC, and a few partner-specific schemas). Calls from customers mix formats: name casing differences (GetUser vs get_user), positional vs named args, typed strings vs JSON-encoded blobs, and sometimes streaming partial bodies. Current adapters are point solutions and cause regressions during rollouts and for streaming tool endpoints.

Goal: Implement a single adapter (Invocation Sanctuary) that: 1) robustly recognizes incoming invocation formats (protocol sniffing), 2) normalizes name/arg shapes to a canonical invocation model, 3) supports progressive streaming of tool request/response payloads with chunk anchoring and idempotent retry semantics, and 4) emits telemetry to help backfill mappings and learning-based alias suggestions.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the fuzzy model-backed name suggestion UI or the canonical registry persistence layer; it focuses on the runtime shim, telemetry hooks, and safe fallbacks for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a single runtime entrypoint that accepts OpenAI-style tool objects and legacy function invocations and returns canonical invocation objects to downstream executors.
Requests with streaming bodies are forwarded to tool endpoints with chunk anchoring; partial outputs are delivered to the client with stable order and resume tokens for retry.
Name mapping rules support 3 strategies: exact, deterministic transform (snake<->camel), and tokenized fuzzy prefix match with a configurable threshold.
Argument coercion rules for common types (ints, floats, timestamps, JSON-strings) applied idempotently and logged when coercion occurs.
Telemetry events emitted for unresolved names and coercions with sample payloads (PII redaction), wired to console tooling for later curation.
Unit + integration tests cover legacy function shapes, OpenAI-style tool shapes, mixed streaming cases, and retry idempotency behavior.
implementation_notes: Create runtime adapter module: invocation_sanctuary.{router, normalizer, stream_bridge} within runtime service.
Protocol sniffing: inspect presence of 'tool' vs 'function' fields, model metadata, and first-chunk tokens to choose parsing path.
Canonical model: {tool_name, canonical_args: dict, metadata: {original_shape, source_protocol_version}} represented as simple dict of strings (no nested typed objects in Linear JSON).
Streaming bridge: add chunk header with 'anchor_id' and 'sequence_index' for out-of-order delivery; generate an idempotency token visible to both client and executor.
Coercion rules: implement pluggable coercion chain (string->int->float->timestamp->json) with opt-out via header 'X-Invocation-Strict'.
Telemetry: sample 1% of invocations by default, fire non-blocking events to telemetry queue with redaction hooks; include resolver decision (exact/transform/fuzzy) as a dimension.
Backwards compatibility: if normalizer fails to find a mapping and original-format executor exists, fall through to legacy executor with a warning header (temporary, to be removed after rollout).
Performance: aim for <1ms median additional latency on non-streamed calls; stream path adds minimal headroom for anchor metadata.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ava Chen: Drafted initial RFC and linked proto for canonical invocation model. Marking P1 due to several incoming customer issues around streaming tool replays.

2026-03-02 - Ravi Patel: Spike completed; prototyped stream_bridge that attaches anchor_id and preserves ordering. Found edge case where chunk boundary splits JSON-encoded arg; added reassembly logic.
2026-03-04 - Design review (Maya Singh): Recommended explicit resume tokens in the client API and console UI flag to surface partial tool results. We'll coordinate with console team for visibility.
2026-03-06 - Security (Jon Park): Reviewed coercion rules; requested mandatory redaction for any field matching known PII patterns before telemetry. Implemented redaction hook in telemetry pipeline.
2026-03-08 - Engineering (Ravi Patel): Implemented fuzzy prefix match using tokenized name comparison. Tuned threshold at 0.75 for our service tests; added override header for strict matching.

2026-03-10 - QA (Elena Morales): Integration tests added for legacy function fallthrough; uncovered a race on retry logic when the executor returns 409 dedupe errors. Will add gating and idempotency reconciliation in next PR.
Action items: (1) Add console flag to surface resolver decisions (PM follow-up). (2) Wire telemetry to runtime-1.22 release dashboard. (3) Patch retry race as separate PR.
risks: Incorrect coercion could change tool semantics; mitigations: strict mode header and conservative default coercion chain.
Streaming anchor metadata may increase payload size and affect low-bandwidth clients; add a feature flag to disable anchoring for specific customers.
Fallback to legacy executors could mask mapping problems; ensure we emit high-cardinality telemetry and run a controlled rollout.
